title: Découverte des sons autour de nous
oneGoal: Students will identify and reproduce simple environmental sounds using their voice
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable making sounds in French or still in silent period?
Do students recognize the difference between loud and soft sounds?
Should I model more sounds or encourage student exploration?
progression: Foundation lesson establishing sound awareness and vocal comfort for future rhythm work
realWorldConnection: Connecting to sounds they hear at home, playground, and in nature

title: Mon corps fait de la musique
oneGoal: Students will create rhythms using body percussion (clapping, tapping, stomping)
decisionPoints: Are students able to maintain a steady beat with their bodies?
Do students need more scaffolding with simple movements first?
Should I introduce call-and-response patterns now?
progression: Builds on sound awareness by adding physical rhythm creation using familiar body parts
realWorldConnection: Like clapping along to favorite songs or marching like soldiers

title: Les animaux chantent aussi
oneGoal: Students will imitate animal sounds with different vocal expressions and rhythms
decisionPoints: Are students connecting animal sounds to rhythm patterns?
Do they need more time exploring vocal variety before adding rhythm?
Should I focus on fewer animals for deeper exploration?
progression: Combines voice work from lesson 1 with rhythm from lesson 2 through familiar animal sounds
realWorldConnection: Connecting to pets, farm animals, or zoo animals they know

title: Répéter comme un écho
oneGoal: Students will echo simple sound and rhythm patterns with increasing accuracy
decisionPoints: Are students ready for 3-4 beat patterns or should I stick to 2 beats?
Do they understand the concept of echoing or need more modeling?
Should I add visual cues to support the auditory patterns?
progression: Develops listening skills and pattern recognition essential for poetry rhythm
realWorldConnection: Like echoing in mountains or repeating after parents

title: Mes premiers mots rythmés
oneGoal: Students will clap the syllables in their own names and simple French words
decisionPoints: Can students hear the beats in their names clearly?
Do they need more practice with familiar words before new vocabulary?
Should I use visual syllable counting to support understanding?
progression: Applies rhythm skills to actual language, bridging sound play to word structure
realWorldConnection: Their own names and words for family members they use daily

title: Comptines simples et mouvements
oneGoal: Students will participate in a simple French nursery rhyme with coordinated movements
decisionPoints: Are students ready for full participation or need more listening time?
Should I simplify movements to focus on rhythm or add complexity?
Do they need the words broken down more before adding actions?
progression: Integrates all previous elements into traditional French cultural expression
realWorldConnection: Like singing games they play with siblings or at daycare

title: Inventer des rythmes ensemble
oneGoal: Students will collaborate to create original rhythm patterns using voice and body
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable taking creative risks in French?
Do they need more structure or are they ready for open exploration?
Should I guide the collaboration more directly or let them lead?
progression: Moves from reproducing patterns to creating original rhythmic expressions
realWorldConnection: Like making up games or songs with friends during play

title: Émotions dans ma voix
oneGoal: Students will express different emotions through vocal tone while maintaining rhythm
decisionPoints: Can students differentiate emotions in vocal expression clearly?
Do they need more emotional vocabulary before rhythm integration?
Should I model more extensively or encourage immediate practice?
progression: Adds emotional expression to rhythm work, preparing for expressive poetry recitation
realWorldConnection: How their voice changes when happy, sad, or excited at home

title: Rimes qui résonnent
oneGoal: Students will identify and create simple rhyming sounds in French
decisionPoints: Do students hear the similar ending sounds in rhymes?
Are they ready to generate rhymes or need more identification practice?
Should I focus on visual rhyme patterns or keep it purely auditory?
progression: Introduces rhyme as a key poetic element while maintaining rhythm focus
realWorldConnection: Like silly word games and rhyming songs they hear in French media

title: Tempo: vite et lentement
oneGoal: Students will perform the same rhythm pattern at different speeds with control
decisionPoints: Can students maintain rhythm accuracy when changing speed?
Do they understand the concept of tempo or need more concrete examples?
Should I add instrumental support or keep it vocal/body only?
progression: Develops rhythmic sophistication and control needed for varied poetic expression
realWorldConnection: Like walking slowly or running fast, or songs that speed up and slow down

title: Ma première performance
oneGoal: Students will perform a simple rhythm and rhyme combination for classmates
decisionPoints: Are students ready to perform individually or need partner support?
Do they need more rehearsal time or are they confident to share?
Should I structure the audience response or let it be natural?
progression: Applies all learned skills in a low-stakes performance setting
realWorldConnection: Like showing family a new song or dance they learned

title: Jouer avec les mots drôles
oneGoal: Students will create and share silly word combinations that maintain rhyme and rhythm
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable being playful with French language?
Do they need prompts for silly ideas or are they generating freely?
Should I encourage more risk-taking or celebrate current attempts?
progression: Builds confidence in creative language use through humor and play
realWorldConnection: Like making up funny words or nonsense songs for entertainment

title: Raconter avec le rythme
oneGoal: Students will tell a simple story using rhythmic speech patterns
decisionPoints: Can students maintain story coherence while focusing on rhythm?
Do they need story prompts or can they create original narratives?
Should I emphasize rhythm or storytelling as the primary focus?
progression: Integrates rhythm into narrative expression, preparing for longer poetic forms
realWorldConnection: Like telling exciting stories with dramatic voices to friends or family

title: Célébrer nos créations
oneGoal: Students will self-assess their growth in rhythm and rhyme while celebrating peer achievements
decisionPoints: Can students articulate what they've learned in French?
Are they able to give constructive feedback to peers?
Should I guide the reflection more or let them lead the celebration?
progression: Reflects on learning journey and builds community around creative expression
realWorldConnection: Like family celebrations of learning to ride a bike or tie shoes

title: Partager notre musicalité
oneGoal: Students will present their favorite rhythm and rhyme creation to a wider audience
decisionPoints: Are students ready for a larger audience or need more preparation?
Should presentations be individual or can they work in groups?
Do they need technical support or can they manage independently?
progression: Culminates core learning with authentic audience and real performance pressure
realWorldConnection: Like school concerts or sharing talents at family gatherings

title: Rythmes du monde francophone
oneGoal: Students will explore rhythm patterns from different French-speaking cultures
decisionPoints: Are students able to distinguish between different cultural rhythm styles?
Do they need more background knowledge about francophone countries?
Should I focus on one culture deeply or survey several briefly?
progression: Extends learning beyond classroom to global French-speaking communities
realWorldConnection: Connecting to diverse music they might hear in their multicultural community

title: Poésie et nature
oneGoal: Students will create nature-inspired poems using environmental sounds and rhythms
decisionPoints: Can students connect natural phenomena to rhythmic patterns?
Do they need more vocabulary about nature or seasons?
Should we go outside for inspiration or use indoor imagination?
progression: Applies poetic skills to meaningful content while connecting to seasonal learning
realWorldConnection: Observing winter weather, birds, and seasonal changes around them

title: Instruments et voix ensemble
oneGoal: Students will combine simple percussion instruments with vocal rhythms
decisionPoints: Can students coordinate instrumental and vocal elements simultaneously?
Do they need more time with instruments before combining with voice?
Should I limit instrument choices or offer full variety?
progression: Adds instrumental dimension to vocal and body percussion mastery
realWorldConnection: Like family music time or joining in with recorded songs using objects

title: Créer un spectacle de classe
oneGoal: Students will collaborate to design and rehearse a class rhythm and poetry showcase
decisionPoints: Are students able to work independently in planning groups?
Do they need more structure in the collaborative process?
Should I assign roles or let them negotiate responsibilities?
progression: Synthesizes all unit learning into collaborative creative project
realWorldConnection: Like organizing family talent shows or community celebrations

title: Notre héritage rythmique
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their growth and plan how to continue using rhythm and poetry in daily life
decisionPoints: Can students articulate specific ways they'll use these skills outside class?
Do they understand the connection between rhythm and language learning?
Should I provide concrete suggestions or let them generate their own plans?
progression: Concludes unit with transfer planning and celebration of growth journey
realWorldConnection: Planning to share skills with family and use rhythm to help with French learning
